body:

## Context
Contracts freeze at Train 1, Tue 1:45am MT. After the freeze only Integration changes `contracts/`, and only by adding things. Before the freeze, three items from Grok's contract review in PR #15 (`pitch/review-log.md`) need settling. Milestone: Train 1.

  - hour beginning h uses EIA hour ending h+1 (`docs/FACTS.md`, Hour conventions);
  - `tools/make_fixture.py` and `research/analysis/demo-story/habit.py` already do exactly that.

  So the map stays, and the -0.2625 and +0.270 t per MW-day pins stand.
- [ ] **Fixture hour 0.** `tools/make_fixture.py` takes hour 0's LMP from `research/analysis/option2/oct/20260930_20261028_PRC_LMP_DAM_20261026_20_37_47_v12.csv`. That row has interval start 2026-10-27T06:00Z, OPR_DT 2026-10-26, HE 24, LMP 30.21857, REAL.
  - Hour-0 fields with no REAL source keep the borrowed value with prov ASSUMPTION.
  - `notes` names every borrowed field.
  - The script regenerates `contracts/fixtures/bundle_2026-10-27.json`; do not edit it by hand.
- [ ] **Pulse life.** Add a comment in `contracts/types.ts` on `pulse_life_yr` and `pulse_cycles_per_yr_budget`. It says:
  - 25 years is the Station lifespan (TORUS_PUBLISHED);
  - it is used as an ASSUMPTION for Pulse's calendar life;
  - so the 300-cycles-a-year budget is an ASSUMPTION.

  No field is renamed or removed.
- [ ] The `contracts/types.ts` header says v1 is frozen at Train 1, with the date.
- [ ] Add this line to the `AGENTS.md` Coordination section: "Before each new issue, read the latest Integration comment on your lane's tracking issue; a `QUEUE:` line there overrides issue order."
- [ ] Tell the engine lane on #3 that fixture hour 0 changed. The DP value on the fixture can move. Lane thresholds cannot: both prices sit inside $21.38 to $55.78 and fall in the shoulder lane.
- [ ] Merge green PRs in lane order per `docs/lanes/integration.md` section 6.1, including #15, #16 and #17 if they are green.

  Local runs use the installed Edge (`channel: "msedge"`).

title: [integration] Offline check: tools/offline-check.mjs that fails on a planted external URL
body:
Queue: core, position 6.

## Context
The stage runs in snapshot mode with no network. The offline check proves it: it serves `dist`, drives the six beats in a real browser, and fails on any request to another origin. It must catch a planted fake URL, or it proves nothing. The design is in `docs/lanes/integration.md` section 6.7. Milestone: Train 2.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `node tools/offline-check.mjs`:
  - serves `dist` on 127.0.0.1 with a built-in `node:http` server;
  - drives beats 1 to 6 through `?beat=N&step=end&motion=off` and each beat's keys;
  - records every request;
  - prints PASS with counts, or FAIL with one line per violation.
- [ ] It fails on each of these:
  - any request to another origin;
  - any WebSocket;
  - any `/api/` request in snapshot mode;
  - a `failed` page state;
  - an external URL in a position the browser would load (`src`, `href`, `url(`, `import(`, `fetch(` and so on) in `dist` html, js or css.

  Other bundled URLs are INFO only.
- [ ] If the app has no `data-beat` hooks yet, the beats report `not built` and the network rule still applies.
- [ ] `--plant` injects `https://planted.offline-check.invalid/...` twice, once as an img and once as a fetch.
  - If both are caught, it prints FAIL lines naming both, then `SELF-TEST OK`, and exits 0.
  - If either is missed, it prints `SELF-TEST BROKEN` and exits 1.
- [ ] Exit codes: 0 PASS, 1 FAIL, 2 `COULD NOT RUN: <reason>` (no dist, no browser, or a server error). Exit 2 is never reported as PASS or FAIL.
- [ ] Vitest `tools/offline-check.test.ts` covers the URL classifier and the origin check. Cases: same origin, other origin, `.invalid`, an SVG namespace (INFO), a data source string (INFO), and `/api/` in snapshot mode.
- [ ] CI gains an `offline` job after `check`. It builds, installs a browser, runs the check, then runs `--plant` and requires `SELF-TEST OK`.

## Files touched
- `tools/offline-check.mjs`
- `tools/lib/*.mjs`, each with a `.d.mts` so `tsc` passes
- `tools/offline-check.test.ts`
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

## How to verify
```bash
npm run build
node tools/offline-check.mjs; echo "exit $?"
node tools/offline-check.mjs --plant; echo "exit $?"
mv dist dist.bak; node tools/offline-check.mjs; echo "exit $? (expect 2)"; mv dist.bak dist
npx vitest run tools/offline-check.test.ts
npm run check:all
```

## Dependencies
The Playwright dev dependency.

Integration runs the data lane's refresh and the engine CLIs, so judging on Wed shows Wed's real plan. Craig is away 6:00 to 11:00pm, so this runs alone.   1. the data refresh command (name per `docs/lanes/data.md`; the plan calls it `prep/refresh_tonight.ps1`);

  3. `npx tsx engine/cli/numbers.ts public/data/bundle_2026-10-28.json`;
  4. the envelope CLI, if separate;
  5. each merged stretch CLI that writes a per-day file;
  6. the engine lane's re-pin command;
  7. the checks.
- [ ] 5:00pm dry run on Oct 27, on `int/refresh-dry` (never merged). Every command runs, and the data step exits non-zero and changes nothing on a forced OASIS failure.
- [ ] At 9:10pm main is green and `int/oct28-refresh` is cut from origin/main.
- [ ] From about 9:16pm, run the data command. Retry every 5 minutes until Oct 28 rows appear; the last try is at 10:00pm.

  - check:all, facts check and offline check are green;

  - peak over trough;

  - the peak leaves the evening.

- [ ] By 10:30pm the refresh is either merged (CI green, or the 10:20pm exception in section 6.5) or abandoned with nothing merged. The outcome goes on #1 and in the run-of-show.
- [ ] Tell Pitch on #5 to regenerate the deck numbers and re-record the video.

Each of these safety constraints gets a source mutation that must turn a test red. Brief: `docs/lanes/engine.md` sections 6.4 and 6.7.

- [ ] `engine/src/site.ts` exports `defaultSite()`: label "Simulated Utah manufacturer", all SIMULATED.

- [ ] `engine/src/inputs.ts` holds the Torus-derived model inputs (19 s ramp, 10C, 0.5C, 6-minute recharge, 7,500 cycles over 25 years), each with its FACTS key in a comment.

  - [ ] the ceiling binds on at least one clear-lane interval (ceiling - host is below the max grid charge)
  - [ ] host is at least `pulse_kw + enrolled_kw` in every interval of HB 17-20
  - [ ] host is at or under the ceiling in every interval

**Context.** Beat 3: a SIMULATED Rocky Mountain Power call lands at 6:40pm MT on a station already discharging. Spin answers alone, while the battery-only ghost misses. **Context.** Torus publishes 7,500 Pulse cycles. Spread over the 25-year Station life, that is a budget of 300 a year (0.82 a day; the 25-year divisor is our assumption).   - [ ] check monotonicity on a $0.50 scan; if it is not monotone, return the smallest feasible scan value, refined by bisection inside that step, and say so in the PR

title: [data] OASIS client, parsers and Mountain-day mapping

Queue: core, position 3.

### Acceptance
- [ ] `prep/oasis.py`: `build_url` for SingleZip and GroupZip (GMT `YYYYMMDDTHH:MM-0000`, start inclusive, end exclusive)
- [ ] `fetch`: at least 5 s between calls (injectable clock); HTTP 429 sleeps 30 s, at most 3 retries then raises; detects error zips (`.xml` member when CSV was asked, or `<m:ERR_CODE>`) and raises `OasisError(code, message)`; caches the raw zip plus `.meta.json` (url, retrieved_utc, sha256, bytes) under `RAW/oasis/<query>/`; a cache hit makes no network call unless `--refetch`
- [ ] Parsers: PRC_LMP DAM v12 (LMP and MCC rows, value column `MW`); SLD_FCST DAM v1 filtered to `TAC_AREA_NAME == "PACE"`; EDAM_WND_SLR_FORECAST_GRP v1 XML (namespace `http://www.caiso.com/soa/EDAMWindAndSolarForecast_v1.xsd`, PACE only, negative solar clamped to 0 and counted). - [ ] `prep/mtday.py`: Mountain day D = 24 UTC hours from D 06:00Z; `local_mt` like `2026-10-27T00:00-06:00`; hour 0 maps to CAISO OPR_DT D-1 OPR_HR 24; fixed UTC-6 with a guard outside May 1 to Oct 31 2026. No `zoneinfo` (this PC's Python raises ZoneInfoNotFoundError for America/Denver)

title: [ui] App shell: stage frame, data loader, stage day and key map
body:
Queue: core, position 1.

### Context
The stage app is an offline, keyboard-driven React page that the judges watch on a projector and on a phone. Vite's root is `app/`, and `public/` is served at `/`. This issue builds the frame every beat sits in: one data loader, the stage day, a scaled 1920x1080 stage, the `DESIGN.md` tokens, the key map and the flags helper. Brief: `docs/lanes/ui.md` section 4, core 1.

**Fold in #14.** The uncommitted work on branch `ui/14-six-beats` (issue #14) goes in here. Cut it down to this issue and the next two (provenance chips, engine client) and land the three as one PR whose body says `Closes #14` plus the three issue numbers.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `app/src/data.ts` is the only module that reads JSON files. It bundles `public/data/bundle_*.json` and `public/derived/*.json` at build time with eager `import.meta.glob`. If Vite refuses imports from the public dir, it falls back to same-origin relative fetches, and the PR says which one it uses. A missing file gives an explicit empty state: never a build failure, never a 0.
- [ ] **Stage day.** It is the `as_of_mt` shared by the day-level keys in `numbers.json`. Until `numbers.json` exists, it is the bundle's `operating_day_mt`. `?day=YYYY-MM-DD` overrides both. A vitest asserts that every day-level key agrees.
- [ ] If the bundle's `operating_day_mt` differs from the stage day, the page shows a failed state that names both files. It never mixes days.
- [ ] **Header.** It shows:
  - the operating day, labeled Today, Tomorrow (day-ahead) or "Cached, from <date>" against the current America/Denver date (inject the clock so tests control it);
  - the node `ELAP_PACE-APND`;
  - "Snapshot, fetched <time> MT", from `fetched_utc`.
- [ ] **Stage frame.** 1920x1080 logical px, scaled by `min(vw/1920, vh/1080)` and letterboxed on `--bg`. Below 768px wide there is no transform: one column, and no sideways scroll at 375px. Hiding overflow does not count as a fix.
- [ ] **Tokens.** `app/src/styles/tokens.css` holds the `DESIGN.md` tokens. Dark is the default, light applies under `prefers-color-scheme: light`, and `?theme=dark|light` overrides both. A vitest compares the token values with the `DESIGN.md` table.
- [ ] **Key map.** `app/src/keymap.ts` is one table that drives both the key handler and the `?` overlay.
  - Core keys: Right/PageDown, Left/PageUp, 1-6, Space, C, E, B, +/-, Home/End, R, ? and Esc.
  - Reserved for stretch: T, D, P, F and I.
  - A vitest fails on any key bound twice in the same context.
  - Keys typed into an input are ignored, except Esc.
- [ ] `app/src/flags.ts` parses `?ff=a,b` (names without the `ff_` prefix), with every flag off by default. It keeps a local list of names until `contracts/flags.ts` lands.
- [ ] **Deep links.** `?beat=1..6&step=start|end` and `?motion=off` work. `document.body` carries `data-beat`, `data-step` and `data-state` (`loading`, `ready`, `playing`, `paused`, `call`, `replanned` or `failed`).

title: [ui] Provenance chips and the one-number rule
body:
Queue: core, position 2.

### Context
Every number on stage must say where it came from, using one of six classes: REAL, DERIVED, SIMULATED, TORUS_PUBLISHED, ASSUMPTION or MEASURED. It must come from `public/derived/numbers.json` (a `StageNumber[]`) or from live engine output, never be typed into the app. This issue builds the components and the tests that enforce that rule. Brief: `docs/lanes/ui.md` sections 4 (core 2) and 6.4.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `<Num k="key" />` renders a StageNumber's `display` string verbatim, with `data-num` and `data-prov` attributes.
  - Its chip text names the class (TORUS_PUBLISHED reads "TORUS PUBLISHED").
  - Its tooltip names `source` and `as_of_mt`.
- [ ] `<Num value display prov source />` renders a live engine value. A `prov` field carried by the data wins. Otherwise:
  - plan values, cycles and envelope values are DERIVED;
  - the host meter and every CrashResult field are SIMULATED;
  - `solve_ms` is MEASURED and is never cached or hard-coded.
- [ ] `<Time>` renders hour and date labels with `data-time`. It formats with `Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { timeZone: "America/Denver" })` or from `hour_mt`/`local_mt`, never the machine's time zone (CI runs in UTC).
- [ ] Four states look different from each other:
  - **loading:** a muted placeholder of the same width;
  - **not computed:** the key or file is absent; dashed outline and the words "not computed";
  - **unavailable:** the data is null; the word "unavailable" and the reason;
  - **failed:** the word "failed" and the file or function name.
  A vitest asserts that a missing key never renders as 0.
- [ ] Numbers use `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` and a reserved min-width in `ch`, so a value change never moves its neighbors. Chips are at least 18px at 1920.
- [ ] `app/src/stageKeys.ts` lists every key each beat reads. A vitest checks each one against `numbers.json` when the file exists; when it does not, the test prints that it skipped and why.
- [ ] **Digit rule vitest.** It renders every registered beat, so later beats are covered with no test edit. Any text node with a digit must sit inside `[data-num]`, `[data-time]`, `[data-axis]` or `[data-copy-ok]`. `[data-copy-ok]` is a short allowlist (P10/P50/P90, schema ids), each entry with a comment.
- [ ] **Copy guard vitest** over `app/src`. It fails on:
  - U+2014 (em dash);
  - comprehensive, robust, seamless, leverage, cutting-edge, game-changer;
  - "Torus lacks", "Torus revenue", "six-minute call", "Utah regulators".
- [ ] `app/src/format.ts` only formats and converts units (kW to MW, seconds to minutes). It never adds, averages or derives a value.
- [ ] A one-line chip legend on the stage explains the six classes in plain words, from `app/src/copy.ts`.

### Files
- `app/src/components/Num.tsx`, `app/src/components/Chip.tsx`, `app/src/components/Time.tsx`
- `app/src/stageKeys.ts`, `app/src/format.ts`, `app/src/copy.ts`
- tests beside each file


PR #15 (branch `grok/pitch`, file `pitch/review-log.md`) is the pitch lane's contract review for the Train 1 freeze. Finding 1 says the fixture's CO2 is shifted one hour late, and that is wrong. title: [pitch] Pitch checker: key resolver and guardrail lint with mutation-checked tests
body:
Queue: core, position 3.

## Context
Every number a judge reads must be a `{key}`, resolved from `public/derived/numbers.json` or from a verified `docs/FACTS.md` row, never typed by hand. PR #17 has a first `pitch/resolve.mjs` with no tests. This issue makes it the lane's guard: one rule module, shared by the copy resolver and the PR scanner. Exit codes:

- 0: clean
- 1: findings
- 2: could not run

## Acceptance
- [ ] **Shared rules** live in `pitch/lib/rules.mjs`. `pitch/resolve.mjs` uses them.
- [ ] **Scope.** It scans `pitch/**/*.md` and `pitch/**/*.html`. It skips `pitch/research-*.md`, `pitch/review-log.md` and `pitch/test/fixtures/**`.
- [ ] **Unknown key.** A `{key}` missing from `pitch/keys.json` fails.
- [ ] **Source "numbers".** A key with `source: "numbers"` reads `display` from `numbers.json`.
  - With `--strict`, a missing key fails.
  - In draft mode the placeholder is allowed, and the run reports the unresolved count.
- [ ] **Source "facts".** A key with `source: "facts"` names a FACTS row in `fact`.
  - The row is VERIFIED, or CONFLICT with the display taken from its say-instead wording.
  - The `display` appears verbatim in the row's Claim or Value cell, or in the matching "Say instead" cell.
  - UNCHECKED and PENDING-ENGINE rows fail.
- [ ] **One source per key.** A key present in `numbers.json` and also marked `source: "facts"` fails.
- [ ] **MEASURED keys** (`solve_ms`, `replan_ms`) never resolve from a file. They render as `[read from screen]`.
- [ ] **`{operating_day}`** resolves to the shared `as_of_mt` of the keys the copy uses, and fails if those keys disagree.
- [ ] **Hand-typed results fail:**
  - `$` amounts
  - percentages
  - a number followed by MW, kW, kWh, MWh, g/kWh, t, ms, s, min, C or x
  - bare numbers of 3 or more digits
- [ ] **Allowlist.** Each entry is a regex with a one-line reason in the code:
  - years 2020 to 2030
  - dates
  - clock times
  - beat timings
  - Schedule 6, 6A and 8
  - IEEE 2030.5
  - `clearlane.envelope/v1`
  - URLs
  - docket numbers
  - slide headings
  - 1920x1080
  - Option 1 and Option 2
  - Train numbers
- [ ] **Dashes.** Em dash (U+2014) and en dash (U+2013) fail.
- [ ] **Banned phrases fail** (case-insensitive). The list is in `docs/lanes/pitch.md` section 7, and includes "Torus lacks", "Torus can't", "Lasso doesn't", "Torus revenue" (unless "not Torus revenue"), "Utah regulators", "six-minute call", "500 MW installed", "Nucleus x", "Startup State", "record peak", "14% to 77%", "Pulse has a 25-year", "27 of 30" and "prices post at".
- [ ] **Hype words fail:** comprehensive, robust, seamless, leverage, cutting-edge, game-changer.
- [ ] **Output.** Each finding prints `file:line: rule: text`.
- [ ] **Flags.** `--render <dir>` writes resolved copies. `--facts <path>` overrides the FACTS.md location (needed until FACTS.md is on `origin/main`).
- [ ] **Tests.** `pitch/test/rules.test.mjs` has one failing and one passing fixture per rule, plus "the current pitch copy exits 0".
- [ ] **Mutation ledger in the PR body.** For each rule:
  1. Before running anything, write down the test you predict will fail.
  2. Break the rule.
  3. Confirm exactly that test fails.
  4. Restore the rule.
- [ ] **Exit 2** on a missing `keys.json`, an unreadable FACTS.md or bad JSON. It never exits 0 in those cases.

- `pitch/resolve.mjs`
- `pitch/lib/rules.mjs`
- `pitch/test/rules.test.mjs`
- `pitch/test/fixtures/**`

```bash

node --test "pitch/test/*.test.mjs"
```

title: [science] Reserve risk: chance a call lands while Spin is refilling (off_reserve_risk)
body:
Queue: stretch-1, position 10.

**Context.** A judge will ask what happens if a second RMP call arrives while Spin is still recharging. This item estimates how often that happens, from Torus's own published 2025 counts, with a closed form checked by a seeded simulation. It ships behind `off_reserve_risk`, which nothing in the six beats reads; the proof-drawer card reads its JSON. Start only after all science core is merged and CORE GREEN is posted on the science tracking issue (or an early start is allowed there). Stop if CORE RED is posted. Merge target: Train 5 (Tue 5:30pm MT).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] The tolerances and the three pinned configs are committed in `science/reserve-risk.md` before computing.
- [ ] Calls are modeled as a non-homogeneous Poisson process with separable hour x weekday rates, from the TORUS_PUBLISHED 2025 counts:
  - by hour: 9, 41, 5, 4, 1, 3, 4, 14, 23, 26, 25, 20, 15, 33, 19, 14, 14, 8, 6, 4, 5, 34, 24, 8
  - by weekday, Mon to Sun: 50, 57, 43, 57, 53, 45, 54
  - under both readings: Mountain, and UTC with MT hour = (h minus 6) mod 24
- [ ] Cases:
  - call duration over a 5 to 6 minute ASSUMPTION band (the published event ran about 5.6 minutes)
  - refill windows of 6 and 12 minutes (Spin discharges fully in 6 minutes and discharges and recharges in 12, TORUS_PUBLISHED)
  - annual totals from 137 (2024) to 359 (2025); using the 2025 shape at 137 is labeled ASSUMPTION
- [ ] For each case:
  - the expected calls a year that start inside a previous call's refill window [s + d, s + d + R], in closed form (integral of lambda x (1 minus exp(minus Lambda over the window)))
  - the chance of at least one per season, with its approximation stated
- [ ] A seeded simulation agrees with the closed form within 3 standard errors on 3 pinned configs.
- [ ] A clustered-arrival stress case, with its clustering rule labeled ASSUMPTION.
- [ ] Refill 0 gives exactly 0 (unit test).
- [ ] Both readings are reported side by side, and the md explains why they give nearly the same count.
- [ ] Once `call-ledger` merges: compare its overlap count at the ledger's own density. Its 359 calls sit on about 180 days, so E scales by N^2/T.
- [ ] `science/reserve_risk.json` records inputs with sha256, seeds, cases and results, keys sorted. Same seed, identical bytes.
- [ ] The doc header says "Flag: off_reserve_risk (not read by the stage app)". No Torus facts beyond the published counts and specs. No em dashes.
